quote: Enhanced circulating visfatin/Nampt levels have been reported in metabolic diseases, such as obesity and type 2 diabetes.
summary: Review of visfatin/Nampt as an adipokine promoting vascular inflammation and atherosclerosis; no UC data.

quote: More recently, however, it has been shown that NAMPT inhibitors do not solely target the tumor but also have an effect on the immune system.
summary: Review of NAMPT inhibitor medicinal chemistry and immune effects, mainly in oncology.

quote: In this review, the knowledge of eNAMPT in cancer will be discussed, focusing on its immunometabolic function as a metabokine, its secretion, its mechanism of action and possible roles in the cancer micro-environment.
summary: Review of extracellular NAMPT as a cytokine-like metabokine in cancer, without UC data.

quote: In addition, a panel of five genes such as ADM, AQP9, CXCL2, IL10 and NAMPT discriminates between all samples from patients with chronic inflammation and healthy controls.
summary: NAMPT mRNA in blood mononuclear cells was one of five genes separating IBD, psoriasis and RA patients from healthy controls.

quote: Because of NAMPT's multiple functions in a variety of physiological processes, their dysregulations have been implicated in the pathogenesis of a number of human diseases or conditions such as acute lung injury, aging, atherosclerosis, cancer, diabetes, rheumatoid arthritis and sepsis.
summary: General review of NAMPT structure and roles in human diseases, with no UC-specific data.

quote: Furthermore, it reviews the evidence that links this protein to some disorders in which myeloid cells have a prominent role (acute infarct, inflammatory bowel disease, acute lung injury and rheumatoid arthritis) and the data showing that inhibition of the enzymatic activity or the neutralization of the cytokine is beneficial in preclinical animal models.
summary: Review of NAMPT in monocyte and macrophage biology, noting preclinical benefit of NAMPT inhibition or neutralization in myeloid disorders including IBD.

quote: We propose that there is a functional equivalent of PNC1 in mammals called Nampt (a.k.a. PBEF/Visfatin), a stress-responsive gene that would coordinately regulate metabolism, cell defenses, and resistance to diseases of aging.
summary: Hypothesis article proposing Nampt as a mammalian longevity regulator; no UC data.

quote: Whereas Nampt(+/-) mice were protected against agonist (isoproterenol and angiotensin II)-induced hypertrophy, Nampt transgenic mice spontaneously developed cardiac hypertrophy at 6 mo of age.
summary: Nampt heterozygous knockout protected and Nampt overexpression caused cardiac hypertrophy in mice, so Nampt is pathogenic in the heart; no intestinal data.

quote: Extracellular PBEF has been shown to increase inflammatory cytokines, such as TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-16, and TGF-β1, and the chemokine receptor CCR3.
summary: Review of PBEF as a proinflammatory cytokine with many immune and metabolic functions; no UC data.

quote: Here, we report that the genetic and pharmacological inhibition of nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (Nampt), the rate-limiting enzyme in the salvage pathway of NAD+ biosynthesis, reduced oxidative stress, inflammation, and keratinocyte DNA damage, hyperproliferation, and cell death in zebrafish models of chronic skin inflammation, while all these effects were reversed by NAD+ supplementation.
summary: Nampt inhibition reduced skin inflammation in zebrafish and lowered psoriasis gene expression in human skin models, so Nampt drives inflammation there; not UC.

quote: NAMPT deficiency in macrophages resulted in HIF-1α destabilization, leading to reduction in M2-like TAM polarization.
summary: Myeloid Nampt deletion reduced immunosuppressive macrophage polarization and boosted antitumour immunity in mouse colorectal cancer; high NAMPT signature predicted poor outcome.

quote: Of note, this newly generated antibody is able to significantly reduce acute and chronic colitis in both DNBS- and dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis.
summary: A neutralizing anti-eNAMPT antibody reduced acute and chronic mouse colitis, eNAMPT administration worsened it, and serum eNAMPT was higher in anti-TNF non-responders.

quote: The increases in the NAD(H) pool inhibited the accumulation of excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and FK866, a specific inhibitor of NAMPT, treatment decreased the CRC nodule size by increasing ROS levels in AOM/DSS mice.
summary: NAMPT is upregulated in colorectal adenoma and cancer, and the inhibitor FK866 shrank tumours in AOM/DSS mice, so NAMPT supports colon tumour growth.

quote: PBEF/NAMPT/visfatin serum levels were increased in patients with IBD, correlated positively with disease activity and negatively with BMD, especially in the lumbar spine.
summary: Serum NAMPT was raised in IBD patients, tracked disease activity and inversely tracked bone density.

quote: Through disruption of NRE1 or pharmacological inhibition, a subset of M1 genes is sensitive to NAMPT activity through its impact on glycolytic processes.
summary: Loss of a STAT1-bound Nampt enhancer in macrophages reduced inflammatory gene expression and increased melanoma burden in mice; no colitis data.

quote: In fact, research has mainly focused on inhibiting the key enzyme of the latter NAD production route, nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT), leading to the identification of numerous inhibitors, including FK866 and CHS-828.
summary: Review of NAD-lowering agents and NAMPT inhibitors for cancer treatment, without UC data.

quote: Highly selective inhibitors of iNOS versus eNOS and neuronal NOS have been identified and some of these have potential in the treatment of a range of inflammatory and other conditions in which iNOS has been implicated.
summary: Review of nitric oxide synthase structure and inhibition, noting selective iNOS inhibitors may treat inflammatory conditions.

quote: Nitrate levels increased in the colonic lumen because epithelial expression of Nos2, the gene encoding inducible nitric oxide synthase, was elevated in the absence of PPAR-γ signaling.
summary: Colonic epithelial Nos2 expression rose when PPAR-γ signalling was lost after antibiotics, raising luminal nitrate and favouring Enterobacteriaceae expansion.

quote: Accumulated data strongly suggest that continuous (chronic) upregulation of pro-inflammatory mediators (e.g., TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6, COX-2, iNOS) are induced during the aging process due to an age-related redox imbalance that activates many pro-inflammatory signaling pathways, including the NF-kappaB signaling pathway.
summary: Review of molecular inflammation in aging that lists iNOS among upregulated pro-inflammatory mediators; no UC data.

quote: Furthermore, HFD induced colonic inflammation, including the increased expression of proinflammatory cytokines, the induction of Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4), iNOS, COX-2, and the activation of NF-κB in the colon.
summary: A high-fat diet increased colonic iNOS expression along with inflammation in mice via TLR4; this is diet-induced, not a colitis model.
NOS here is part of PDD-NOS (pervasive developmental disorder not otherwise specified), not the NOS2 gene.
NOS appears only as a generic nitric oxide synthase mention among curcumin targets in head and neck cancer, not as NOS2 specifically.

quote: Most importantly, GMSCs were capable of immunomodulatory functions, specifically suppressed peripheral blood lymphocyte proliferation, induced expression of a wide panel of immunosuppressive factors including IL-10, IDO, inducible NO synthase (iNOS), and cyclooxygenase 2 (COX-2) in response to the inflammatory cytokine, IFN-gamma.
summary: iNOS is one of several immunosuppressive factors induced in gingival mesenchymal stem cells that ameliorate mouse colitis; iNOS itself was not tested.

quote: Exposure of LPS-activated macrophages to 6-ethyl chenodeoxycholic acid (6E-CDCA; INT-747) a synthetic FXR ligand, results in a reciprocal regulation of NF-kappaB dependent-genes (TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6, COX-1, COX-2, and iNOS) and induction of SHP, a FXR-regulated gene.
summary: iNOS is one of several NF-kB genes repressed by an FXR agonist in macrophages; the paper's focus is FXR in colitis.

quote: Activated macrophages are described as classically activated or M1 type and alternatively activated or M2 type, depending on their response to proinflammatory stimuli and the expression of genetic markers including iNOS, arginase1, Ym1, and Fizz1.
summary: iNOS is used only as an M1 macrophage marker in a study of Akt1 and Akt2 in polarization and DSS colitis.
